title: Tomatoes, whole, canned, solids and liquids, with salt added

content.title: About
content.content: Tomatoes, whole, canned, solids and liquids, with salt added (5802) are ripe tomatoes that have been heat‑processed and sealed in glass or metal jars. Salt is added to enhance flavor and preserve the product. Canned tomatoes retain most of their nutrients, a characteristic sweet‑tart taste, and a soft texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Canning allows tomatoes to be stored for years without loss of flavor.
Tomatoes are one of the world’s most popular vegetables and are a base for sauces, soups, and stews.
Salt in canned tomatoes helps stabilize the fruit’s structure and inhibits microbial growth.
Tomatoes canned in their own juice contain less added fat than those packed in oil.
Thermal processing increases the bioavailability of lycopene, a powerful antioxidant.

items.title: Rich in lycopene
items.content: Lycopene is a strong antioxidant that may reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease and certain cancers.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains vitamin A and beta‑carotene
items.content: Vitamin A is essential for vision, skin health, and immunity.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Canned tomatoes fit well into low‑fat dietary patterns.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The added salt may be a concern for people with hypertension; low‑salt versions are preferable.

items.title: Bisphenol A in packaging
items.content: Metal cans can contain trace amounts of BPA; glass jars are a safer alternative when available.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use canned whole tomatoes in sauces, soups, stews, pasta dishes, pizza, salads, or simply heat them as a side. Their soft texture and rich flavor make them ideal for a wide range of recipes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, transfer leftovers to an airtight container, refrigerate, and consume within 3–5 days. Discard if you notice mold, off‑odors, or other signs of spoilage.
